title: The return (Ezra 1)
hookLine: Cyrus of Persia lets the exiles go home to rebuild
carry: the ones who go and the ones who send

cards: "Thus saith Cyrus king of Persia." A proclamation goes out through a whole empire, spoken aloud and put in writing.
The God of heaven, says the king, has given him all the kingdoms of the earth, and charged him to build a house in Jerusalem, in Judah. Then the line that opens the way home.
In the King James words: "Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem." After all the chapters of loss, the book of Ezra opens with a door.

teach.h: GOD STIRRED UP A FOREIGN KING.
teach.b: The book opens by saying why: it was "in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that the word of the LORD by the mouth of Jeremiah might be fulfilled," and "the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus."
A foreign king, and the text sees God moving through him anyway. Help, again, from an unexpected place. Now listen to the shape of the decree.

teach.h: LET HIM GO UP: AN INVITATION.
teach.b: It's an invitation: let him go up. Not everyone does. The ones who rose up to go, the text says, were all those whose spirit God had stirred.
Others stay, and the text doesn't scold them.

The people around them help instead, strengthening the travelers with silver and gold, goods and animals, and freewill offerings for the house of God. A return needs both: the ones who go and the ones who send.
Then Cyrus does one more thing.
He brings out the vessels of the house of the LORD that Nebuchadnezzar had carried off from Jerusalem, counts them out to a leader of Judah, and sends them home.
A few days ago, in Daniel, a king drank wine from vessels like these. Now they're packed for the road. The return doesn't begin with a wall or a Temple.
It begins with going up, and carrying back what was taken.

how: Moving to the land of Israel is called aliyah, going up, the same picture of going up that Cyrus's decree uses, and Jews who move to Israel today are said to make aliyah.

o: a march back to Egypt, retracing the Exodus
going home to Jerusalem at Cyrus's invitation
the Temple vessels being carried off to Babylon

p: king of Persia who sends them home
sent silver, gold, goods and animals

s: Cyrus orders every Jew in his kingdom back to Jerusalem
he says "let him go up": an invitation. those whose spirit God had stirred went.
Cyrus sends back the Temple vessels Nebuchadnezzar had taken
he brings them out and has them counted to a leader of Judah.
the people around the travelers did nothing to help
they strengthened the travelers with silver, gold, goods and animals.

games.q: you're an exile in Babylon. the decree is read aloud: let him go up to Jerusalem. you've built a life here. what does Ezra 1 say people did?
o: those whose spirit God stirred went, and others helped them go.
no one went until the Temple was rebuilt.
games.why: the ones whose spirit was stirred went up, and the neighbors who stayed sent them off with gifts. both are part of the return.

practice: Think of something of yours that got left somewhere along the way: a song your family sang, a recipe nobody makes anymore, a language you grew up hearing, a skill you set down.
Don't scold yourself for the distance, the decree didn't; just hold it the way an exile might hold the name of a city, and find the first small step that would carry it back.
If you pray, ask in words from your tradition for your spirit to be stirred.

wordCard.voice: The return. Cyrus's decree in Ezra 1: let him go up to Jerusalem, and build the house of the LORD. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: and let him go up, from Cyrus's decree in Ezra 1:3.

carryVoice: Your line: the ones who go and the ones who send. Cyrus invited; he didn't order. That's day eight hundred seventy-four.
